title: Southern Ring Nebula (NIRCam Image)
caption: The Southern Ring Nebula, NGC 3132, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3132 · constellation Vela · about 2500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, and the Webb ERO Production Team

recognition.text: Official ESA/Webb press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Jagged rings of gas and dust surround a bright central star, pierced by hundreds of straight, brightly lit lines that stream through gaps in the nebula like sunlight through breaks in a cloud. The center is set off in teal, and transparent red regions reveal distant galaxies behind. This is NGC 3132, the Southern Ring Nebula, a planetary nebula seen by Webb in near-infrared light.

The bright central star is not the nebula's source. That role belongs to a second, dimmer star, which you can just make out at lower left on one of the bright star's spikes. Over thousands of years it has cast off at least eight shells of gas and dust.

The two stars are locked in a tight orbit. As they circle each other, the dimmer star sprays material in many directions, while the brighter one stirs up turbulence. Together they create these intricate rings.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.42 x 2.25 arcminutes) and distance (2500 light years), the frame spans roughly 1.8 × 1.6 light-years. Its light set out about 2,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image from Webb's NIRCam shows a 0.9-micron filter in blue, hydrogen's Paschen-alpha line in cyan, molecular hydrogen at 2.12 microns in green, a 3.56-micron filter in yellow, and hydrogen's Brackett-alpha line with molecular hydrogen at 4.7 microns in red.
understand.eye: Most of this light is infrared and invisible to the eye, and the diffraction spikes on bright stars come from Webb's optics.

explore: Deeper teal in the center marks denser gas and dust that light cannot escape. The bright angled line at upper left is a faraway galaxy seen edge-on, and the smallest, reddest galaxies are the most distant or the dustiest.
NIRCam was built by the University of Arizona and Lockheed Martin's Advanced Technology Center.
alt: Jagged rings of gas around a bright central star, crossed by straight bright lines, with a teal center and red outer regions dotted with distant galaxies.
